stepClassification.explanation: Build a SteeringBody snapshot from the example’s current position, velocity and limits.
Call scene-engine seek and arrive on the same body and target. The displayed desired velocity reproduces Arrive’s readout only; acceleration always comes from the engine call.
Select the candidate named by arrivalEnabled. This selection is an explicit toy policy, with no claim to implement blending or arbitration.
The local fixed-step movement loop uses engine add, scale and clipLength to update velocity then position. It omits the scene’s boundary, drag and rest-snap behaviour.

studies.executableNullRationale: The executable is not null: the model runs the described selection and integration mechanism using real engine Seek and Arrive outputs. It does not claim that the whole family is one algorithm.
studies.rxjsRationale: Null because streams add no explanatory value to choosing and applying a steering request at fixed simulation steps.
handWorkedSpecClaims: The first step requests acceleration 4 and moves from x 0, velocity 0 to x 0.25, velocity 1.
At x 14.25, velocity 6, Seek requests 4; Arrive desires 111/19 and requests -12/19. The Arrive update reaches x 597/38.
Default Arrive remains short of the depot and inside its target radius at the end; the one-input Seek comparison reaches a maximum x of 28.5, then acquires negative velocity.
At the depot with velocity 2, zero Seek output preserves motion; Arrive instead requests braking.
Record parameters, mechanism-block alignment, nearby ids, all frame placeholders, deterministic output and drawing bounds are asserted by the written spec.
limitations: One straight, unobstructed route; the model demonstrates two family members and explicit selection, not simultaneous composition or route planning.
Independent comparison runs are distinguished from the candidate arrows evaluated on one current state.
No scene field boundaries or exact rest snap; the teaching loop is declared local.

stepClassification.explanation: A readonly local SteeringOutput pairs linear and angular acceleration and samples a fixed-duration pulse. The engine has no combined output record or angular steering primitive.
The local consumer adds linear acceleration times the interval to current velocity using engine add and scale.
Update angular velocity by scalar acceleration times the same interval. No angular integrator is provided by the engine.
Advance position and heading with the updated rates. Linear requests remain in world coordinates; orientation does not redirect them.

studies.executableNullRationale: The executable is not null: the module executes the record’s pulse producer and complete linear/angular consumer. This is explicitly a local teaching mechanism for a data structure, not an engine steering primitive.
studies.rxjsRationale: Null because a fixed pulse and state update already expose the data boundary; no asynchronous stream behaviour is under study.
handWorkedSpecClaims: The first 0.25 s update changes velocity (2,0) to (2,0.5), rotation to 0.125, position to (0.5,0.125) and heading to 0.03125.
At 1 s both output channels become zero, while velocity remains (2,2) and rotation remains 0.5. Position is (2,1.25) and heading is 0.3125.
At 4 s the default state reaches position (8,7.25), heading 1.8125, with unchanged coasting rates.

Changing only world-y acceleration to zero keeps y at zero while every heading and rotation sample remains identical. Changing the initial heading also leaves the world-coordinate linear update unchanged.
A coarser interval changes integrated position and heading despite matching end-of-pulse velocities; a pulse ending between samples remains active to the next boundary.
Record parameters, mechanism-block alignment, nearby ids, all frame placeholders, deterministic output and offered-input drawing bounds are asserted by the written spec.
limitations: No drag, speed limit, collision response or heading-dependent actuator; the choice of consumer is explicit throughout.
The output’s units and coordinate convention require producer/consumer agreement; the data shape cannot enforce them.
Pulse timing is sampled and the rates-first integrator has a time-step-dependent position and heading.
